catalyst_text: Reported positive preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results from the AURORAS-1 trial in RAS-mutant solid tumors showed favorable safety and tolerability, linear pharmacokinetics, and both confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses across multiple tumor types. Early activity observed at doses as low as 8 mg once daily supports continued clinical development and potential best-in-class differentiation.
catalyst_text_evidence: Erasca is evaluating ERAS-0015 in the AURORAS-1 Phase 1 trial in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. Early dose escalation data in AURORAS-1 demonstrated favorable safety and tolerability results, well-behaved, linear PK, and confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses in multiple patients across multiple tumor types with different RAS mutations, including confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses at doses as low as 8 mg once daily (QD).

catalyst_text: Reported positive preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy data in second-line KRAS G12X pancreatic cancer showed uORR of 40% at 16–32 mg QD and 42% at 24–32 mg QD, with 50% uORR at 32 mg QD. These results indicate meaningful activity in a hard-to-treat population.
catalyst_text_evidence: PDAC At PADs of 16-32 mg QD, 40% uORR14wk (N=20) in 2L KRAS G12X PDAC, which exceeded comparator by 11 percentage points5,6 At RDEs of 24-32 mg QD, 42% uORR14wk (N=12) in 2L KRAS G12X PDAC, which exceeded comparator by 13 percentage points5,6 At RDE of 32 mg QD, 50% uORR14wk (N=2) in 2L KRAS G12X PDAC, which exceeded comparator by 15 percentage points5,7

drug_indication: KRAS G12X Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
catalyst_text: Reported positive preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy results in KRAS G12X NSCLC showed strong activity, including uORR of 62% in 2L+ and 75% in post-ICI/platinum cohorts at 16–32 mg QD, and 64% uORR at 24–32 mg QD. Safety was generally well-tolerated with mostly low-grade adverse events and no dose-limiting toxicities reported to date.
catalyst_text_evidence: Efficacy: Robust monotherapy overall response rates (ORR) in patients with KRAS G12X non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and with KRAS G12X pancreatic cancer (PDAC), in each case as of the relevant data cutoff (DCO)1,2: NSCLC At PADs of 16-32 mg QD, 62% uORR8wk (N=37) in second line or greater (2L+) KRAS G12X NSCLC, which exceeded comparator by 24 percentage points3,4 At PADs of 16-32 mg QD, 75% uORR8wk (N=16) in post-ICI/platinum (2/3L) KRAS G12X NSCLC, which exceeded comparator by 37 percentage points3,4 At recommended doses for expansion (RDEs) of 24-32 mg QD, 64% uORR8wk (N=25) in 2L+ KRAS G12X NSCLC3 Safety and Tolerability: Generally well-tolerated with mostly low-grade adverse events (AEs), no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), low rate of dose interruptions or reductions due to treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs), and no discontinuations due to TRAEs

catalyst_text: Reported encouraging Phase 1 combination dose escalation data
detailed_catalyst_text: Early Phase 1 combination data with panitumumab in metastatic colorectal cancer showed no DLTs in N=3 and an unconfirmed partial response in the efficacy-evaluable patient. These findings support the feasibility of combining with standard-of-care anti-EGFR therapy.
catalyst_text_evidence: Preliminary data suggest ERAS-0015 may combine safely with standard-of-care doses of panitumumab with no DLTs as of DCO (N=3) and 1/1 uPR in CRC Combinability: ERAS-0015 showed promising clinical potential to combine with panitumumab (anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody) No DLTs observed through the 2026-03-31 DCO (N=3) with 1 unconfirmed partial response (uPR) in 1 efficacy-evaluable patient with metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC)

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 1 monotherapy expansion and combination cohorts
detailed_catalyst_text: Monotherapy expansion and combination dose escalation cohorts in the U.S. Phase 1 program were initiated. Starting these cohorts ahead of prior guidance advances clinical development and broadens safety and efficacy assessment across tumor types.
catalyst_text_evidence: Key Upcoming and Completed Milestones The Company initiated ERAS-0015 monotherapy expansion and combination dose escalation cohorts in the US (in Q2 2026 and Q1 2026, respectively), both ahead of previous guidance.
